docs.title: NavSim opens but ROS is disconnected
docs.text:
• Confirm that rosbridge is still running on port 9090.
  • Confirm that NavSim contains the correct host or IP address.
  • Source both ROS 2 and the built ubm-fsae workspace before starting rosbridge.
  • Confirm that the selected landmark format matches the message package in the sourced workspace.
  • Open the browser developer tools with Ctrl+Shift+I and inspect the Console.

docs.title: Changes to JavaScript or CSS do not appear
docs.text: Open the browser developer tools, enable Disable cache in the Network tab, keep the developer tools open, and refresh with Ctrl+F5.

docs.title: Track edits disappear
docs.text: Tracks stored only in browser local storage are not portable and can be lost when browser data is cleared. Use Save to export important tracks to JSON or CSV files.

docs.title: Unity Formula Student Driverless Simulator
docs.text:
The UBM Formula Student Driverless Simulator is a Unity-based 3D front end for the ubm-fsae ROS 2 stack. It loads cone tracks, renders the Formula Student vehicle and environment, receives the vehicle pose from ROS, and publishes simulated LiDAR, stereo-camera, cone, and transform data.

The simulator can also run without ROS. In standalone mode, the vehicle can be driven with a keyboard, gamepad, or joystick, which is useful for inspecting a track, validating sensor settings, and measuring simulator performance before connecting the complete pipeline.

Typical uses include:

  • visualizing the vehicle on Formula Student cone tracks;
  • testing the perception pipeline with simulated point clouds and stereo camera data;
  • receiving localization output from /ekf_pose/odom and applying it to the simulated vehicle;
  • checking TF, sensor frames, topic names, rates, and payload sizes;
  • evaluating different LiDAR sampling and stereo-camera configurations;
  • reproducing tests with bundled TrackGen/NavSim maps;
  • running manual driving sessions, cone-impact tests, and timed laps.

UNITY_SIM_SCREENSHOT_01 — Simulator overview

Replace this note with a screenshot of the running simulator showing the vehicle, track, cone counter, session timer, Settings button, and diagnostic HUD. Suggested file: docs/assets/unity-simulator/runtime-overview.png.

Use: ![Unity simulator runtime overview](site:/assets/unity-simulator/runtime-overview.png)

docs.title: How the simulator fits into the ROS pipeline
docs.text:
The Unity simulator supports two communication transports:

  • ROS-TCP-Connector, the default transport, using a ROS-TCP-Endpoint on the ROS 2 computer;
  • ROS#, the fallback transport, using rosbridge over a WebSocket.

Both transports expose the same simulator topics to the rest of the stack.

                    odometry input
ROS 2  ------------------------------------>  Unity vehicle pose
       /ekf_pose/odom

ROS 2  <------------------------------------  Unity simulated sensors
       /lidar_points, /camera_data, /cones, /tf

Unlike NavSim, the Unity simulator does not publish simulated odometry. In ROS odometry mode it subscribes to odometry and uses it to position the vehicle. It then produces sensor data from that pose and the 3D scene.

The simulator does not currently calculate complete vehicle dynamics. Standalone movement is kinematic, and ROS mode follows received odometry. Cone collisions use lightweight Unity rigidbodies and are not a validated Formula Student impact model.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Unity Hub;
  • Unity Editor 6000.6.0f1;
  • Git and Git LFS;
  • network access while Unity resolves packages from Git;
  • for ROS integration, an Ubuntu 24.04 system running ROS 2 Jazzy and a built ubm-fsae workspace.

The required Unity version is recorded in the project's ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt. Do not downgrade the project to the old 6000.0.32f1 version. The current version is newer than the fixed Unity baseline for CVE-2025-59489.

docs.title: Download and open the project
docs.text:
Install and initialize Git LFS before cloning. Vehicle FBX and Blender files are stored through LFS:

git lfs install
git clone https://github.com/ubm-driverless/ubm-fsae-sim.git
cd ubm-fsae-sim
git lfs pull

Avoid downloading the project as a GitHub source ZIP: depending on the archive configuration, large model files may be downloaded as small LFS pointer files instead of real assets.

Open Unity Hub and:

  1. install Unity 6000.6.0f1 if it is not already available;
  2. select Add -> Add project from disk;
  3. choose the cloned ubm-fsae-sim directory;
  4. open the project with Unity 6000.6.0f1;
  5. wait for Unity Package Manager and asset import to finish;
  6. open Assets/Scenes/MainMenu.unity;
  7. enter Play mode.

The project includes ROS-TCP-Connector, ROS#, URP, the Input System, and the other Unity packages in Packages/manifest.json. They are resolved when the project is opened for the first time.

If an FBX or .blend file contains only text beginning with version https://git-lfs.github.com/spec/v1, close Unity and run:

git lfs pull

UNITY_SIM_SCREENSHOT_02 — Unity project and Play button

Replace this note with a screenshot of Unity showing the Project panel, Assets/Scenes/MainMenu.unity, and the Play button. Suggested file: docs/assets/unity-simulator/unity-editor-start.png.

Use: ![Opening the Unity simulator project](site:/assets/unity-simulator/unity-editor-start.png)

docs.title: Start a standalone simulation
docs.text:
ROS is optional for a standalone session.

  1. Open Assets/Scenes/MainMenu.unity and enter Play mode.
  2. Select an Athena or Visione vehicle.
  3. Select the display LOD. LOD 1 is the recommended default.
  4. Select the number of LiDAR vertical layers and points per layer.
  5. Choose one of the bundled tracks.
  6. Choose the asphalt preset. Time-of-day options are currently saved placeholders and do not yet provide a complete environment change.
  7. Click Start Simulation.
  8. Press Esc, open Controls, and select Standalone input.
  9. Drive with W/A/S/D or the arrow keys.

Standalone input uses simplified kinematic movement. It is intended for simulator interaction and sensor testing, not vehicle-dynamics validation.

docs.title: Connect ROS 2
docs.text: The transport is selected from Settings -> ROS connection after the simulation starts.

docs.title: ROS-TCP-Connector
docs.text:
ROS-TCP-Connector is the default transport. On the ROS 2 computer:

  1. install ROS-TCP-Endpoint in the same workspace as ubm_interfaces;
  2. build the workspace;
  3. source ROS 2 and the workspace;
  4. start ROS-TCP-Endpoint on a network interface reachable from the computer running Unity, using port 10000 by default.

Follow the ROS 2 setup instructions in the official ROS-TCP-Endpoint repository for the exact installation and launch commands supported by the installed version.

In Unity:

  1. press Esc;
  2. open ROS connection;
  3. select ROS-TCP-Connector;
  4. set ROS-TCP host/IP to the ROS computer's address;
  5. keep port 10000 unless the endpoint uses another port;
  6. click Retry connection;
  7. check the connection status at the top of the page.

127.0.0.1 works only when Unity and ROS-TCP-Endpoint share the same host network. When Unity runs on Windows and ROS runs on another Ubuntu computer, enter the Ubuntu computer's LAN address.

docs.title: ROS# and rosbridge fallback
docs.text:
ROS# communicates through rosbridge. In a terminal where ROS 2 and the built ubm-fsae workspace are sourced, start rosbridge:

source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
cd /path/to/your/ubm-fsae-workspace
source install/setup.bash
ros2 launch rosbridge_server rosbridge_websocket_launch.xml port:=9090

In Unity:

  1. open Settings -> ROS connection;
  2. select ROS# fallback;
  3. set the rosbridge URL, for example ws://localhost:9090 or ws://<ROS_HOST_IP>:9090;
  4. click Retry connection.

The workspace containing ubm_interfaces must be sourced before starting rosbridge; otherwise the bridge cannot advertise the custom camera message.

UNITY_SIM_SCREENSHOT_03 — ROS connection page

Replace this note with screenshots of the ROS-TCP and ROS# transport selections, including endpoint fields and connected status. Suggested file: docs/assets/unity-simulator/ros-connection.png.

Use: ![Unity simulator ROS connection settings](site:/assets/unity-simulator/ros-connection.png)

docs.title: Select ROS odometry control
docs.text:
Connecting a transport does not automatically change the vehicle input mode. Open Settings -> Controls and select ROS odometry. The default input is:

Topic Type Purpose /ekf_pose/odom nav_msgs/msg/Odometry UBM FSAE vehicle pose

The ROS connection page provides two shortcuts:

  • UBM FSAE topic selects /ekf_pose/odom;
  • Legacy sim topic selects /command_odom.

Verify the selected input on the ROS system:

ros2 topic info /ekf_pose/odom
ros2 topic echo /ekf_pose/odom --once

docs.title: Published ROS interfaces
docs.text:
Defaults are loaded from Assets/StreamingAssets/default_settings.json and can be changed at runtime.

Direction Default topic Message Purpose Subscribe /ekf_pose/odom nav_msgs/msg/Odometry Vehicle position and orientation Publish /lidar_points sensor_msgs/msg/PointCloud2 Simulated LiDAR point cloud Publish /cones visualization_msgs/msg/MarkerArray Visible/noisy/missing cone simulation Publish /camera_data ubm_interfaces/msg/CameraData Left/right images and camera information Publish /tf tf2_msgs/msg/TFMessage Vehicle and sensor transforms

The point cloud is normally published in the hesai_lidar frame. Vehicle and sensor frame names can be edited from ROS connection -> Frames.

Useful checks include:

ros2 topic hz /lidar_points
ros2 topic hz /camera_data
ros2 topic echo /tf --once
ros2 topic echo /cones --once

The optional DriveSubscriber understands ubm_interfaces/msg/Control on /control, but it is currently diagnostic. Vehicle movement in ROS mode still follows odometry.

docs.title: Launch menu
docs.text: The launch menu configures the session before the simulation scene is loaded.

docs.title: Vehicle and display LOD
docs.text:
• Athena and Visione select the vehicle model and matching sensor arrangement.
  • LOD 0 High uses the most detailed display mesh.
  • LOD 1 Medium is the default and recommended general-purpose choice.
  • LOD 2 Low reduces rendering cost on slower computers.

The collision mesh remains separate from the selected visual LOD.

docs.title: LiDAR sampling
docs.text:
• Vertical layers controls the number of simulated scan layers.
  • Points per layer controls horizontal sampling.
  • The summary displays the total points generated per scan.

Dense scans increase CPU work, message size, serialization cost, and network traffic. Start with a smaller configuration when testing on a low-spec laptop.

docs.title: Track and environment
docs.text:
The track selector shows a top-down preview, cone counts, dimensions, format, and start position. Bundled JSON and CSV maps are read from Assets/StreamingAssets/.

The environment section selects an asphalt material. Time-of-day selections are stored for future use but are currently placeholders.

UNITY_SIM_SCREENSHOT_04 — Launch menu

Replace this note with a screenshot of the complete launch menu, including vehicle, LOD, LiDAR sampling, track preview, and environment settings. Suggested file: docs/assets/unity-simulator/launch-menu.png.

Use: ![Unity simulator launch menu](site:/assets/unity-simulator/launch-menu.png)

docs.title: Runtime Settings menu
docs.text: Press Esc or click Settings to open the runtime panel. Vehicle input and camera interaction are paused while the panel is open. Values are saved in Unity PlayerPrefs when the panel closes.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Overview summarizes the ROS connection, active camera, graphics status, vehicle position, and diagnostics. It also links to maps, controls, ROS, and the main launch menu.

docs.title: Maps
docs.text: Maps searches and loads bundled tracks without restarting Play mode. It can also load a CSV or TrackGen/NavSim JSON file using an absolute filesystem path. Selecting a map does not activate it until Load selected map is pressed.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text: Controls switches between standalone input and ROS odometry and configures maximum speed, acceleration, and steering rate for standalone motion.

docs.title: ROS connection
docs.text: ROS connection selects the transport and endpoint, retries or closes the connection, edits topic names, selects odometry presets, configures TF frequency, and changes vehicle/sensor frame names.

docs.title: Sensors
docs.text:
Sensors enables or disables the point cloud, cone, and stereo-camera publishers. Disabling unused publishers is the fastest way to reduce simulator load during movement-only tests.

The point-cloud section controls:

  • topic and field/layer definition files;
  • horizontal angular resolution and vertical-layer count;
  • maximum distance and scan frequency;
  • visualization of rays that hit cones.

The cone-detection section controls topic, mesh markers, distance, frequency, missing detections, noisy detections, and maximum position noise.

The stereo-camera section controls topic, publication frequency, image size, raw or JPEG payload, and JPEG quality. The available per-eye profiles are 1280×720, 960×540, 640×360, and 426×240.

UNITY_SIM_SCREENSHOT_05 — Sensor settings

Replace this note with a screenshot of the Sensors page showing publisher toggles, LiDAR parameters, and stereo-camera profiles. Suggested file: docs/assets/unity-simulator/sensor-settings.png.

Use: ![Unity simulator sensor settings](site:/assets/unity-simulator/sensor-settings.png)

docs.title: Camera
docs.text:
The simulator provides four display views:

  • Chase follows the vehicle from behind;
  • Overhead follows the position while keeping a fixed world orientation;
  • Orbit rotates around and follows the vehicle;
  • Free roam detaches the camera for independent scene inspection.

The page also controls overhead height/framing, orbit distance, orbit-axis inversion, and follow smoothing.

docs.title: Graphics
docs.text:
Graphics provides Low, Balanced, and High runtime profiles, along with target FPS, VSync, URP render scale, real-time shadows, and the performance HUD. Graphics API selection requires restarting Unity; on Linux, use -force-vulkan if the OpenGL editor backend produces rendering artifacts.

UNITY_SIM_SCREENSHOT_06 — Runtime Settings tabs

Replace this note with an annotated screenshot identifying Overview, Maps, Controls, ROS connection, Sensors, Camera, and Graphics. Suggested file: docs/assets/unity-simulator/runtime-settings-tabs.png.

Use: ![Unity simulator Settings tabs](site:/assets/unity-simulator/runtime-settings-tabs.png)

docs.title: Tracks and map formats
docs.text:
Bundled tracks belong in Assets/StreamingAssets/. Supported files appear in both the launch menu and the runtime map library and are included in standalone builds.

The simulator supports:

  • TrackGen/NavSim JSON;
  • typed CSV with start, blue, yellow, orange, and big rows;
  • legacy x,y CSV files, loaded as unknown cones.

A typed CSV example is:

start,0.0,0.0,0.0
blue,5.0,2.0
yellow,5.0,-2.0
orange,0.0,1.0

TrackGen/NavSim JSON preserves initialPosition, cones, path, and significant positions. Unity currently instantiates the cones and applies the initial pose; path and significant-position data are accepted for compatibility but are not used for Unity path following.

Unity uses x/z as the ground plane, while TrackGen and ROS use x/y:

TrackGen/ROS Unity x x y z positive yaw negative Unity yaw around y

Press R to place the vehicle at the active map's start pose. If the map has no start pose, the simulator uses the scene's initial vehicle position.

UNITY_SIM_SCREENSHOT_07 — Map library and track

Replace this note with a composite image showing a map selected in the runtime library and the corresponding cone track in the scene. Suggested file: docs/assets/unity-simulator/map-library.png.

Use: ![Unity simulator map library](site:/assets/unity-simulator/map-library.png)

docs.title: Driving, cone impacts, and run timing
docs.text:
In standalone mode, W/S controls throttle and brake/reverse, while A/D steers. Arrow keys are aliases. Gamepads and generic joysticks are supported.

Track cones can be knocked over. Each cone impact is counted once. Press Shift+R or use the cone HUD reset button to restore every cone and clear the counter.

Press T to start or stop the run timer. The timer uses unscaled Unity time, so it continues to measure consistently across frame-rate changes.

docs.title: Cameras
docs.text: Press C to cycle through Chase, Overhead, Orbit, and Free roam views.

docs.title: Overhead
docs.text: Use the mouse wheel to change altitude and orthographic framing. With a gamepad, the vertical left stick changes height; use the triggers for vehicle throttle while this camera is active.

docs.title: Orbit
docs.text: Use the mouse wheel to change distance. Drag with the left mouse button or use the gamepad right stick to orbit around the vehicle.

docs.title: Free roam
docs.text: Drag with either mouse button to look around. Use W/A/S/D to move on the horizontal plane, E/Q to move vertically, and hold Shift for precise slow movement. Vehicle keyboard input is disabled while Free roam is active.

docs.title: Keyboard and mouse shortcuts
docs.text:
Input Action Esc Open or close runtime Settings C Cycle Chase, Overhead, Orbit, and Free roam cameras W/A/S/D or arrows Drive in standalone mode R Respawn at the active map start pose Shift+R Restore all cones and clear the impact counter T Start or stop the session timer F3 Show or hide the performance/ROS diagnostics HUD L Show or hide LiDAR rays that hit cones Mouse wheel Change Overhead height or Orbit distance Left-mouse drag Rotate the Orbit camera Either-mouse drag Look around in Free roam W/A/S/D in Free roam Move the detached camera horizontally E/Q in Free roam Move the detached camera up/down Shift in Free roam Precise slow camera movement Alt+F4 Close a standalone Linux/Windows player

Vehicle and free-roam input are paused while Settings is open. Shortcut handlers also ignore focused text fields where applicable.

docs.title: Performance and diagnostics
docs.text:
Press F3 to open the diagnostics HUD. It reports:

  • FPS, frame time, and Unity/managed memory;
  • LiDAR and camera publish cadence, payload size, and transmit age;
  • odometry receive and application counts;
  • odometry message age and recent message intervals;
  • source motion and vehicle tracking error;
  • vehicle ground clearance.

If performance is poor:

  1. disable unused publishers in Sensors;
  2. reduce LiDAR layers, points per layer, or scan frequency;
  3. reduce stereo resolution or frequency;
  4. enable JPEG payloads when network bandwidth is the bottleneck;
  5. select the Low or Balanced graphics profile;
  6. reduce URP render scale or disable real-time shadows.

Raw stereo images and dense point clouds are expensive to render, serialize, and transmit. The camera publisher keeps at most one stereo capture in flight and drops missed periods instead of building an unbounded queue.

docs.title: Build a standalone player
docs.text:
In Unity, open File -> Build Profiles and create or select the target platform profile. The scene order must contain:

  1. Assets/Scenes/MainMenu.unity;
  2. Assets/Scenes/scene.unity.

Build into a directory outside Assets/. Generated Unity directories such as Library, Temp, Logs, Builds, and UserSettings must not be committed.

docs.title: Unity cannot connect to ROS
docs.text:
• Confirm that the selected transport matches the server running on the ROS computer.
  • For ROS-TCP, verify the endpoint address and port 10000.
  • For ROS#, verify the WebSocket URL and rosbridge port 9090.
  • Use the ROS computer's LAN IP when Unity runs on another machine.
  • Ensure ubm_interfaces is built and sourced before starting the endpoint or rosbridge.
  • Check firewall rules for the selected TCP port.

docs.title: The vehicle does not move in ROS mode
docs.text:
• Select ROS odometry under Controls.
  • Select the UBM FSAE topic preset or set /ekf_pose/odom manually.
  • Run ros2 topic echo /ekf_pose/odom --once.
  • Open the F3 HUD. ODOM: STALE indicates that Unity is not receiving fresh messages.
  • If messages arrive but tracking error grows, investigate pose application or coordinate conversion.

docs.title: A custom message cannot be advertised
docs.text: Build and source the matching ubm_interfaces package in the same ROS environment as ROS-TCP-Endpoint or rosbridge, then restart the server.

docs.title: The project opens with missing vehicle meshes
docs.text: Install Git LFS, close Unity, run git lfs pull, and reopen the project.

docs.title: Linux rendering artifacts
docs.text: Restart the Unity Editor or standalone player with -force-vulkan. Graphics API selection is not changed by the runtime graphics profile.

docs.title: Simulator Connection and Integration Guides
docs.text:
This section contains focused procedures for connecting the Unity and NavSim simulators to ROS 2, rosbridge, ROS-TCP-Endpoint, Foxglove, and multi-computer test environments.

  • Unity, NavSim, ROS 2 and Foxglove explains the available transports and the recommended combined architecture.
  • Integrated Unity and p5.js TrackSim test describes a local odometry integration test.
  • NavSim on Ubuntu and Unity on Windows adapts the odometry test to two computers.
  • Unity Windows, ROS 2 Ubuntu and visualization covers ROS-TCP, Camera WebGUI, and Foxglove visualization.

For simulator installation, features, menus, and normal operation, return to the main Simulator Guides.

docs.title: Unity, NavSim, ROS 2 and Foxglove
docs.text:
This guide describes two ways to connect the Unity simulator and the browser-based NavSim to one ROS 2 Jazzy graph:

  • ROS# / rosbridge: legacy WebSocket transport used by older Unity configurations.
  • ROS-TCP-Connector / ROS-TCP-Endpoint: the recommended Unity transport for camera and LiDAR traffic.

The examples assume that Unity runs on Windows, while ROS 2, NavSim and Foxglove run on Ubuntu. Replace the example addresses with the addresses of the current network.

docs.title: Transport overview
docs.text:
NavSim browser ── WebSocket :9090 ──► rosbridge ──► ROS 2 graph
                                                       ▲       │
                                                       │       ▼
Unity ── TCP :10000 ──► ROS-TCP-Endpoint ─────────────┘  pipeline / telemetry

NavSim never communicates directly with Unity. It publishes ROS messages through rosbridge; ROS-TCP-Endpoint forwards matching ROS messages to Unity and receives Unity sensor data into the same ROS graph.

Typical topic directions are:

Topic Publisher Consumer /ekf_pose/odom NavSim Unity and ROS nodes /camera_landmark_array NavSim ROS perception/SLAM nodes /lidar_landmark_array NavSim ROS perception/SLAM nodes /lidar_points Unity ROS LiDAR pipeline and telemetry /camera_data Unity ROS camera pipeline and telemetry /control ROS nodes Unity

All ROS processes participating in one test must use the same ROS_DOMAIN_ID. The examples use 42.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Set the workspace path once in every new terminal:

export UBM_WS=/path/to/ubm-fsae
source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
source "$UBM_WS/install/setup.bash"
export ROS_DOMAIN_ID=42

When cloning the ROS-TCP-enabled branch, initialize its submodules and build the required packages first:

cd "$UBM_WS"
git submodule update --init --recursive
colcon build --symlink-install --packages-select ubm_interfaces ros_tcp_endpoint

ubm_interfaces is required by rosbridge and live telemetry to load custom types such as LandmarkArray and CameraData.

docs.title: Recommended setup: Unity over ROS-TCP
docs.text: Use this mode when Unity sends point clouds or camera frames. It avoids JSON/WebSocket conversion of high-bandwidth sensor messages.

docs.title: Terminal 1 — ROS-TCP Endpoint
docs.text:
export UBM_WS=/path/to/ubm-fsae
source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
source "$UBM_WS/install/setup.bash"
export ROS_DOMAIN_ID=42

ros2 launch launch/ros_tcp_endpoint.launch.py \
  tcp_ip:=0.0.0.0 \
  tcp_port:=10000

In Unity select ROS-TCP-Connector, then configure:

TCP host: <Ubuntu Ethernet IP>
TCP port: 10000

For example, when Ubuntu is 10.42.0.1, Unity uses 10.42.0.1:10000. Do not use 127.0.0.1 when Unity and ROS run on different computers.

docs.title: Terminal 2 — rosbridge for NavSim
docs.text:
NavSim runs in a browser on Ubuntu, so rosbridge should listen only on loopback. This prevents external clients from using it and avoids exposing port 9090 unnecessarily.

export UBM_WS=/path/to/ubm-fsae
source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
source "$UBM_WS/install/setup.bash"
export ROS_DOMAIN_ID=42

ros2 launch rosbridge_server rosbridge_websocket_launch.xml \
  address:=127.0.0.1 \
  port:=9090

The current NavSim configuration uses ws://localhost:9090.

rosbridge does not deserialize and forward every ROS topic automatically. It only creates a ROS subscription and converts payload data when a WebSocket client explicitly subscribes to a topic. NavSim currently publishes odometry and landmark messages; it does not subscribe to Unity's /lidar_points or /camera_data. Therefore these high-bandwidth messages do not pass through rosbridge in this setup.

Do not use the topics_pub_glob / topics_sub_glob command-line examples unless they have been validated with the installed rosbridge version. On ROS 2 Jazzy, passing YAML-style lists through the standard XML launch file can turn the arguments into STRING_ARRAY parameters and make rosbridge exit. The loopback-only bridge plus NavSim's publisher-only behavior is the supported default.

docs.title: Terminal 3 — NavSim web server
docs.text:
cd /path/to/ubm-trackgen-navsim-js
python3 -m http.server 8085 --bind 127.0.0.1

Open http://localhost:8085, select Navigation, then press Reconnect ROS if the browser page was already open when rosbridge started.

docs.title: Terminal 4 — optional Foxglove live telemetry
docs.text:
live_telemetry_node is the preferred in-repository path for Foxglove. It processes /camera_data and /lidar_points before sending them over WebSocket on port 8765; the default configuration resizes and JPEG-compresses camera data and applies point-cloud processing.

export UBM_WS=/path/to/ubm-fsae
source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
source "$UBM_WS/install/setup.bash"
export ROS_DOMAIN_ID=42

ros2 run live_telemetry_node live_telemetry_node \
  --ros-args \
  --params-file "$UBM_WS/launch/live_telemetry_node.yaml"

In Foxglove Studio connect to:

ws://<Ubuntu Ethernet IP>:8765

If Foxglove runs on Ubuntu, use ws://localhost:8765.

docs.title: Legacy setup: Unity over ROS# / rosbridge
docs.text: Use this mode only for compatibility with an older Unity scene configured for ROS#. It is suitable for low-bandwidth topics such as odometry, but it is not recommended for raw stereo images or point clouds because rosbridge serializes messages for WebSocket transport.

docs.title: Terminal 1 — rosbridge accessible from Unity
docs.text:
export UBM_WS=/path/to/ubm-fsae
source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
source "$UBM_WS/install/setup.bash"
export ROS_DOMAIN_ID=42

ros2 launch rosbridge_server rosbridge_websocket_launch.xml \
  address:=0.0.0.0 \
  port:=9090

In Unity select ROS# fallback and configure:

Rosbridge URL: ws://<Ubuntu Ethernet IP>:9090

Unity must use the Ubuntu IP address, not localhost or 127.0.0.1.

NavSim can use this same bridge when it runs on Ubuntu. Its browser URL remains ws://localhost:9090.

docs.title: Terminal 2 — optional Foxglove live telemetry
docs.text: Use the same live_telemetry_node command shown in the ROS-TCP setup. It is independent of the Unity transport.

docs.title: Terminal 3 — NavSim web server
docs.text:
cd /path/to/ubm-trackgen-navsim-js
python3 -m http.server 8085 --bind 127.0.0.1

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Open another terminal, source the same workspace and domain, then use the commands appropriate for the current test:

export UBM_WS=/path/to/ubm-fsae
source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
source "$UBM_WS/install/setup.bash"
export ROS_DOMAIN_ID=42

ros2 topic hz /ekf_pose/odom
ros2 topic hz /lidar_points
ros2 topic hz /camera_data
ros2 topic info -v /lidar_points
ros2 topic info -v /camera_data

For point-cloud metadata, use one-off queries instead of printing the complete point cloud:

ros2 topic echo /lidar_points --once --field width
ros2 topic echo /lidar_points --once --field height
ros2 topic echo /lidar_points --once --field point_step
ros2 topic echo /lidar_points --once --field header.frame_id

For the custom camera message, first confirm that it is alive without printing image bytes:

ros2 topic hz /camera_data
ros2 topic info -v /camera_data

docs.title: Network and firewall
docs.text:
Find Ubuntu's active IPv4 addresses with either command:

ip -4 -br addr
hostname -I

Check whether UFW is enabled:

sudo ufw status numbered

Only open the port required by a remote client. Prefer a rule restricted to the Windows IP address.

Scenario Required rule Unity uses ROS-TCP sudo ufw allow from <WINDOWS_IP> to any port 10000 proto tcp Unity uses legacy ROS# sudo ufw allow from <WINDOWS_IP> to any port 9090 proto tcp Foxglove runs on Windows sudo ufw allow from <WINDOWS_IP> to any port 8765 proto tcp

The NavSim web server and loopback-only rosbridge do not need firewall rules because they listen only on 127.0.0.1.

Avoid broad rules such as sudo ufw allow 9090/tcp unless every device on the local network is trusted and needs access. Do not open these ports on a public router.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Check Resolution NavSim shows a connection error Terminal 2 must show that rosbridge started on 9090 Confirm WS_URL is ws://localhost:9090, then click Reconnect ROS rosbridge cannot import ubm_interfaces.msg ros2 interface show ubm_interfaces/msg/LandmarkArray Build ubm_interfaces, then source install/setup.bash before starting rosbridge Unity cannot connect over ROS-TCP Endpoint output and the Windows host/port Start the endpoint on 0.0.0.0:10000; configure Unity with the Ubuntu IP; check UFW Unity works but NavSim odometry is missing ros2 topic hz /ekf_pose/odom Verify NavSim is in Navigation mode and uses the same ROS_DOMAIN_ID through its rosbridge server Foxglove has no camera or LiDAR data ros2 topic hz /camera_data and /lidar_points Start live_telemetry_node from a sourced workspace; check the Foxglove URI uses port 8765

docs.title: Test integrato Unity e p5.js TrackSim
docs.text: Il progetto ubm-trackgen-navsim-js può essere usato come sorgente autonoma lightweight: il path follower muove l'auto nel simulatore 2D e pubblica la sua posa come odometria ROS 2. Unity può sottoscrivere direttamente questa odometria e riprodurre il movimento dell'auto nella scena principale.

docs.title: Configurazioni da raccordare
docs.text:
Componente WebSocket Topic odometria p5.js TrackSim ws://localhost:9091 /ekf_pose/odom Unity ws://localhost:9090 /command_odom

Per il test descritto qui non occorre modificare i repository: si usa un solo rosbridge sulla porta 9091, un proxy TCP locale dalla porta 9090 alla 9091 e si cambia il topic dell'odometria dal menu Unity.

docs.title: 1. Avviare rosbridge
docs.text:
Nel terminale A:

source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
source /home/andrearosnvme/DRIVERLESS_2026/ubm-fsae-slam/install/local_setup.bash
export ROS_DOMAIN_ID=42
export ROS_AUTOMATIC_DISCOVERY_RANGE=LOCALHOST

ros2 launch rosbridge_server rosbridge_websocket_launch.xml \
  address:=127.0.0.1 \
  port:=9091

L'overlay ubm-fsae-slam contiene anche ubm_interfaces, necessario per i messaggi landmark pubblicati dal simulatore p5.js.

docs.title: 2. Rendere rosbridge raggiungibile da Unity
docs.text:
Nel terminale B:

socat \
  TCP-LISTEN:9090,bind=127.0.0.1,reuseaddr,fork \
  TCP:127.0.0.1:9091

Questo comando non crea un secondo ROS bridge: inoltra le connessioni Unity dalla porta 9090 alla porta 9091.

docs.title: 3. Avviare il simulatore p5.js
docs.text:
Nel terminale C:

cd /home/andrearosnvme/DRIVERLESS_2026/ubm-trackgen-navsim-js
python3 -m http.server 8085 --bind 127.0.0.1

Aprire nel browser http://localhost:8085, quindi:

  1. Controllare che ROS risulti CONNECTED; altrimenti premere Reconnect ROS.
  2. Aprire Tracks e premere Load.
  3. Caricare, per esempio, cones_JSON/LoongLoop_V02.json.
  4. Passare a Navigation, oppure premere N.
  5. Selezionare Path follower, oppure premere 3.
  6. Impostare inizialmente una velocità di circa 2–3 m/s.
  7. In Sensors > Odometry Settings, impostare Noise a 0 per evitare oscillazioni visive dell'auto Unity.

LoongLoop_V02.json contiene 155 coni, 77 punti di traiettoria e una posa iniziale. Per un test ancora più leggero si può usare DV_Acceleration.json, che contiene 70 coni e 17 punti.

docs.title: 4. Avviare Unity con Vulkan
docs.text:
Rosbridge e socat devono essere già attivi prima di premere Play in Unity.

Nel terminale D:

/mnt/Storage_HDD/Unity/Editors/6000.6.0f1/Editor/Unity \
  -projectPath /mnt/Storage_HDD/Projects/ubm-fsae-sim \
  -force-vulkan

Aprire Assets/Scenes/scene.unity, quindi:

  1. Premere Play.
  2. Premere Esc per aprire il menu.
  3. Nel campo Athena Odom sostituire /command_odom con /ekf_pose/odom.
  4. Premere Invio oppure fare clic fuori dal campo.
  5. Se il movimento non parte immediatamente, fermare e riavviare Play: il valore viene conservato nei PlayerPrefs.

docs.title: 5. Verificare l'odometria ROS 2
docs.text:
In un terminale facoltativo:

source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
source /home/andrearosnvme/DRIVERLESS_2026/ubm-fsae-slam/install/local_setup.bash
export ROS_DOMAIN_ID=42
export ROS_AUTOMATIC_DISCOVERY_RANGE=LOCALHOST

ros2 topic info /ekf_pose/odom --verbose
ros2 topic echo /ekf_pose/odom --once
ros2 topic hz /ekf_pose/odom

La frequenza attesa con le impostazioni predefinite è circa 10 Hz.

docs.title: Comportamento atteso e limitazioni
docs.text:
• Unity riceve la posa dell'auto, ma non importa automaticamente pista, path o coni creati nel simulatore p5.js. L'auto segue quindi le coordinate del TrackSim sopra la scena Unity esistente.
  • La conversione degli assi è già implementata: Unity X = -ROS Y e Unity Z = ROS X.
  • Al primo messaggio l'auto Unity può teletrasportarsi alla posa iniziale della pista p5.js; è il comportamento previsto.
  • Il TrackSim pubblica attualmente uno twist nullo, ma Unity usa direttamente posizione e orientamento, quindi il movimento funziona ugualmente.
  • L'odometria viene pubblicata solamente quando il TrackSim è in modalità Navigation, non in modalità Editing.
  • Se il browser viene rallentato quando passa in background, anche movimento e pubblicazione possono diventare meno regolari. Conviene tenerlo visibile accanto a Unity.
  • La modalità Nearest cones non è ancora implementata; per il test autonomo va usato Path follower.
  • Per alleggerire Unity si possono disattivare temporaneamente multi_scan e gli altri sensori. Non va disattivato l'oggetto principale athena_with_multi_scan, che contiene OdomSubscriber, Rigidbody e il collegamento ROS.

docs.title: Miglioramento successivo
docs.text: Una configurazione stabile dovrebbe uniformare porta WebSocket e topic dell'odometria nei due simulatori. In questo modo non sarebbero più necessari né socat né il cambio manuale del topic dal menu Unity.

docs.title: Test odometria: NavSim su Ubuntu e Unity su Windows
docs.text: Questa guida adatta il test locale UNITY_P5JS_ODOMETRY_TEST.md a due PC. Il browser con TrackGen/NavSim, ROS 2 Jazzy e rosbridge girano su Ubuntu 24.04; Unity gira su Windows. È un test della sola odometria prima della pipeline FSAE completa. Non servono Vulkan, WSL, Docker, socat o un secondo rosbridge.

docs.title: Configurazione
docs.text:
Componente PC Indirizzo Ruolo TrackGen/NavSim nel browser Ubuntu ws://localhost:9090 Pubblica /ekf_pose/odom rosbridge Ubuntu 0.0.0.0:9090 Riceve P5 e Unity Unity Windows ws://IP_UBUNTU:9090 Sottoscrive /ekf_pose/odom Server web P5 Ubuntu http://localhost:8085 Serve lo sketch al browser Ubuntu

Sostituire IP_UBUNTU con l'IPv4 reale della scheda Wi-Fi o Ethernet Ubuntu, per esempio 192.168.1.42. localhost in Unity indica Windows; localhost nello sketch aperto nel browser Ubuntu indica Ubuntu. Solo TCP 9090 deve essere raggiungibile da Windows. Entrambi i PC possono essere sulla stessa Wi-Fi o collegati allo stesso router via cavo. Con un cavo diretto senza DHCP potrebbero servire IP statici nella stessa sottorete.

docs.title: 1. Impostare la porta nello sketch P5 su Ubuntu
docs.text:
Nella copia Ubuntu di TrackGen/NavSim, aprire sketch.js e usare:

const WS_URL = "ws://localhost:9090";
const ODOM_TOPIC_NAME = "/ekf_pose/odom";

La seconda riga è già corretta nella versione esaminata. P5 e Unity useranno così un solo rosbridge sulla 9090, senza inoltro 9090 → 9091. In alternativa si può lasciare P5 sulla 9091 e configurare sia rosbridge sia Unity sulla 9091: neppure in quel caso serve socat. Dopo la modifica ricaricare la pagina con Ctrl+F5, se necessario disattivando la cache del browser.

docs.title: 2. Avviare rosbridge su Ubuntu — terminale A
docs.text:
Il percorso dell'overlay viene dal test precedente; correggerlo se la directory Ubuntu è diversa.

source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
source /home/andrearosnvme/DRIVERLESS_2026/ubm-fsae-slam/install/local_setup.bash
export ROS_DOMAIN_ID=42
export ROS_AUTOMATIC_DISCOVERY_RANGE=LOCALHOST

ros2 launch rosbridge_server rosbridge_websocket_launch.xml \
  address:=0.0.0.0 port:=9090

Lasciare aperto questo terminale. L'indirizzo 0.0.0.0 consente a Unity di raggiungere rosbridge tramite l'IP Ubuntu; 127.0.0.1 accetterebbe solo client locali. La discovery ROS 2 su LOCALHOST va bene per questo test: i client P5 e Unity parlano WebSocket con rosbridge, mentre il nodo ROS resta su Ubuntu. Se poi si aggiungono nodi ROS su altri host, rivalutare tale variabile. Non avviare un altro rosbridge sulla stessa porta.

docs.title: 3. Avviare NavSim su Ubuntu — terminale B
docs.text:
cd /home/andrearosnvme/DRIVERLESS_2026/ubm-trackgen-navsim-js
python3 -m http.server 8085 --bind 127.0.0.1

Aprire nel browser Ubuntu http://localhost:8085, quindi:

  1. Verificare ROS CONNECTED, altrimenti premere Reconnect ROS.
  2. In Tracks > Load scegliere LoongLoop_V02.json o DV_Acceleration.json da cones_JSON.
  3. Passare a Navigation (N) e scegliere Path follower (3).
  4. Impostare inizialmente 2–3 m/s e mettere Sensors > Odometry Settings > Noise a 0.

Lo sketch pubblica /ekf_pose/odom come nav_msgs/Odometry circa ogni 100 ms solo in Navigation. Nelle copie locali esaminate, LoongLoop_V02.json e DV_Acceleration.json sono identici fra P5 e Unity: scegliere lo stesso nome nei due programmi aiuta a confrontare la posa.

docs.title: 4. Verificare Windows → Ubuntu
docs.text:
Su Ubuntu trovare l'IP della scheda realmente collegata:

ip -4 -br addr

Usare l'indirizzo Wi-Fi/Ethernet, non 127.0.0.1 o un IP Docker 172.x.x.x. Da PowerShell Windows:

Test-NetConnection 192.168.1.42 -Port 9090

Sostituire l'IP di esempio. TcpTestSucceeded : True conferma che la porta è raggiungibile. Se è False, controllare indirizzo, rete, rosbridge e firewall. Se UFW è attivo, autorizzare solo Windows sostituendo IP_WINDOWS:

sudo ufw status
sudo ufw allow from IP_WINDOWS to any port 9090 proto tcp

Non inoltrare 9090 dal router verso Internet: rosbridge qui è destinato alla LAN fidata. Su Wi-Fi ospiti, controllare che non sia attivo l'isolamento fra client.

docs.title: 5. Collegare Unity su Windows
docs.text:
Aprire Unity normalmente, senza opzioni Vulkan. Aprire Assets/Scenes/MainMenu.unity, entrare in Play, scegliere per esempio LoongLoop_V02.json e LOD 1, poi avviare la simulazione.

  1. Premere Esc e aprire ROS.
  2. In Rosbridge URL scrivere ws://IP_UBUNTU:9090; premere Invio o uscire dal campo.
  3. Premere Retry connection. Se era già connesso a un altro bridge, prima Disconnect.
  4. Verificare Odometry input = /ekf_pose/odom. Se è rimasto /command_odom da vecchi test, premere UBM FSAE topic.
  5. In Controls scegliere ROS odometry: la connessione WebSocket, da sola, non cambia la modalità di guida.

La scena Unity contiene ancora connector serializzati con ws://localhost:9090: all'avvio può comparire un warning su localhost anche se l'URL remoto è salvato nei PlayerPrefs. Retry connection applica l'URL configurato ai connector. Attendere che lo stato ROS mostri i connector connessi prima di verificare il movimento.

docs.title: 6. Verifica ROS 2 facoltativa — terminale C su Ubuntu
docs.text:
Usare lo stesso ambiente del terminale A:

source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
source /home/andrearosnvme/DRIVERLESS_2026/ubm-fsae-slam/install/local_setup.bash
export ROS_DOMAIN_ID=42
export ROS_AUTOMATIC_DISCOVERY_RANGE=LOCALHOST

ros2 topic info /ekf_pose/odom --verbose
ros2 topic echo /ekf_pose/odom --once
ros2 topic hz /ekf_pose/odom

L'ultimo comando continua fino a Ctrl+C; la frequenza attesa è circa 10 Hz. Questo terminale serve solo per diagnosi: non c'è più alcun terminale socat.

docs.title: Risultato atteso e problemi comuni
docs.text:
• Windows non raggiunge 9090: verificare su Ubuntu con ss -lntp | grep ':9090' che rosbridge ascolti su 0.0.0.0, poi controllare IP, firewall e isolamento della rete.
  • P5 CONNECTED, Unity offline: in Unity serve ws://IP_UBUNTU:9090, non localhost; terminare l'editing del campo e premere Retry connection.
  • Unity connesso, auto ferma: controllare P5 in Navigation e Path follower, ros2 topic echo, topic Unity /ekf_pose/odom e Controls su ROS odometry.
  • Posa inattesa: il primo messaggio può spostare l'auto Unity alla posa iniziale P5. Unity non importa automaticamente coni, pista o path dal browser. Il subscriber usa Unity X = -ROS Y e Unity Z = ROS X.
  • Movimento irregolare: azzerare il noise, mantenere attivo il browser P5 e iniziare senza sensori pesanti. Lo sketch invia uno twist nullo, ma Unity usa posizione e orientamento.
  • Errori su altri topic: per questa prova conta /ekf_pose/odom; tenere sourced l'overlay ROS se si testano anche i messaggi custom di camera o LiDAR.

docs.title: Unity Windows ↔ ROS 2 Ubuntu: ROS-TCP e visualizzazione
docs.text:
Questa guida descrive il collegamento tra il simulatore Unity sul PC Windows e ROS 2 Jazzy sul PC Ubuntu, collegati direttamente via Ethernet.

Macchina Indirizzo Ethernet Ubuntu / ROS 2 10.42.0.1 Windows / Unity 10.42.0.2

docs.title: Architettura
docs.text:
ROS-TCP, rosbridge e Foxglove Bridge sono tre servizi distinti. Nessuno avvia automaticamente gli altri.

Unity (Windows)
  │
  ├── ROS-TCP, TCP 10000 ──────────────► ROS 2 (Ubuntu)
  │                                        │
  │                                        ├── rosbridge, WebSocket 9090 ─► Camera WebGUI
  │                                        │
  │                                        └── Foxglove Bridge, WebSocket 8765 ─► Foxglove Studio
  │
  └── TCP host configurato: 10.42.0.1

ROS-TCP-Endpoint riceve i messaggi binari inviati dal connettore Unity e li pubblica/sottoscrive sul grafo ROS 2. Non è un server WebSocket e non sostituisce né rosbridge né Foxglove Bridge.

docs.title: Workspace di test isolato
docs.text:
Il workspace dedicato è:

/home/andrearosnvme/DRIVERLESS_2026/ros-tcp-test

Contiene:

  • src/ros_tcp_endpoint: ROS-TCP-Endpoint ufficiale, branch ROS 2, versione 0.7.0;
  • src/ubm_interfaces: collegamento simbolico a ubm-fsae/ubm_interfaces, quindi non è una copia e non modifica il repository ubm-fsae;
  • build, install e log: artefatti della compilazione ROS 2.

Il workspace è stato compilato con ROS 2 Jazzy e fornisce sia ros_tcp_endpoint sia il tipo custom ubm_interfaces/msg/Control.

docs.title: 1. Avviare il ROS-TCP Endpoint
docs.text:
In un terminale Ubuntu:

cd /home/andrearosnvme/DRIVERLESS_2026/ros-tcp-test
source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
source install/setup.bash
ros2 run ros_tcp_endpoint default_server_endpoint --ros-args \
  -p ROS_IP:=0.0.0.0 \
  -p ROS_TCP_PORT:=10000

L'output atteso contiene:

Starting server on 0.0.0.0:10000

0.0.0.0 ascolta su tutte le interfacce di Ubuntu, inclusa quella Ethernet 10.42.0.1.

docs.title: Configurazione Unity
docs.text:
Nella pagina ROS del simulatore selezionare ROS-TCP-Connector e impostare:

TCP host: 10.42.0.1
TCP port: 10000

Non usare 127.0.0.1: dal PC Windows indicherebbe Windows stesso, non Ubuntu.

docs.title: 2. Verificare che Unity pubblichi sul grafo ROS 2
docs.text:
In un secondo terminale:

cd /home/andrearosnvme/DRIVERLESS_2026/ros-tcp-test
source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
source install/setup.bash

ros2 topic list -t
ros2 topic info -v /camera_data
ros2 topic hz /camera_data
ros2 topic hz /lidar_points

Durante il test sono stati osservati questi topic Unity:

/camera_data  [ubm_interfaces/msg/CameraData]
/lidar_points [sensor_msgs/msg/PointCloud2]
/tf           [tf2_msgs/msg/TFMessage]

/camera_data ha un publisher Unity attivo e una frequenza di circa 3,3 Hz. Il messaggio contiene due immagini annidate, left_image e right_image, oltre a telemetria IMU, magnetometro e sensori ambientali.

docs.title: 3. Visualizzare /camera_data con Camera WebGUI
docs.text: ubm-camera-webgui usa rosbridge, non ROS-TCP. Perciò rosbridge deve rimanere avviato separatamente.

docs.title: Avviare rosbridge
docs.text:
In un terzo terminale Ubuntu:

cd /home/andrearosnvme/DRIVERLESS_2026/ros-tcp-test
source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
source install/setup.bash
ros2 launch rosbridge_server rosbridge_websocket_launch.xml \
  address:=0.0.0.0 port:=9090

È importante caricare install/setup.bash: rosbridge deve conoscere il messaggio custom ubm_interfaces/msg/CameraData.

docs.title: Avviare la pagina WebGUI
docs.text:
cd /home/andrearosnvme/DRIVERLESS_2026/ubm-camera-webgui
python3 -m http.server 8086

Se il browser gira su Ubuntu, aprire:

http://localhost:8086

La pagina tenta automaticamente ws://localhost:9090.

Se il browser gira su Windows, aprire:

http://10.42.0.1:8086/?rosbridge=ws://10.42.0.1:9090&topic=/camera_data

La GUI mostra le immagini sinistra/destra, la frequenza dei messaggi e un grafico degli arrivi degli ultimi dieci secondi.

docs.title: 4. Visualizzare /lidar_points con Foxglove
docs.text:
Per Foxglove è preferibile Foxglove Bridge, più efficiente di rosbridge per i point cloud.

cd /home/andrearosnvme/DRIVERLESS_2026/ros-tcp-test
source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
source install/setup.bash
ros2 launch foxglove_bridge foxglove_bridge_launch.xml

Foxglove Bridge ascolta sulla porta 8765. In Foxglove Studio selezionare Open connection → Foxglove WebSocket e usare:

ws://10.42.0.1:8765

Su Ubuntu, se Foxglove Studio è locale, è equivalente ws://localhost:8765.

Per il LiDAR aggiungere un pannello 3D, quindi abilitare:

  • /lidar_points;
  • /tf.

/lidar_points è un sensor_msgs/msg/PointCloud2, che Foxglove visualizza nativamente nel pannello 3D. Se la nuvola non appare, verificare il frame nel messaggio e la disponibilità della relativa trasformazione su /tf.

docs.title: 5. Visualizzare /camera_data con Foxglove
docs.text:
Il pannello standard Image di Foxglove accetta un'immagine top-level (sensor_msgs/msg/Image, sensor_msgs/msg/CompressedImage o schema Foxglove equivalente). /camera_data non compare in quel selettore perché è un messaggio custom che contiene le immagini nei campi left_image e right_image.

Questo non indica un problema di pubblicazione: per controllare ROS 2 si usa:

ros2 topic hz /camera_data

Il repository locale delle estensioni è:

/home/andrearosnvme/DRIVERLESS_2026/ubm-foxglove-extensions

La copia locale usa come remoto ufficiale:

https://github.com/ubm-driverless/ubm-foxglove-extensions.git

L'estensione pertinente è proto_camera_data_panel. Aggiunge il pannello Camera Data Viewer, che visualizza immagini stereo, IMU e metriche del messaggio camera.

docs.title: Compilare e installare il pannello Camera Data Viewer
docs.text:
Sono necessari Node.js e npm. Dopo averli installati:

cd /home/andrearosnvme/DRIVERLESS_2026/ubm-foxglove-extensions/proto_camera_data_panel
npm install
npm run build
npm run local-install

Riavviare Foxglove Studio oppure premere Ctrl+R, aggiungere Camera Data Viewer e configurare il topic /camera_data.

Al momento della stesura di questa guida Node.js/npm non erano installati sulla macchina, quindi l'estensione non è ancora compilata né installata in Foxglove.

docs.title: Porte e firewall
docs.text:
Porta Servizio Necessaria da Windows? TCP 10000 ROS-TCP Endpoint Sì, per Unity TCP 9090 rosbridge Solo se la Camera WebGUI gira su Windows TCP 8765 Foxglove Bridge Solo se Foxglove gira su Windows TCP 8086 Server HTTP della Camera WebGUI Solo se la pagina viene aperta da Windows

Se UFW è attivo, consentire solo le porte effettivamente necessarie. Esempio per ROS-TCP:

sudo ufw allow from 10.42.0.2 to any port 10000 proto tcp

Applicare lo stesso schema a 9090, 8765 e 8086 solo quando il relativo client è sul PC Windows.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: This guide explains how documentation generation is configured and works across the repositories listed in repositories.yaml.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The repository uses a combination of tools for generating documentation:

  • MkDocs: For managing the overall documentation website.
  • MkDocstrings: To parse Python docstrings and generate reference pages.
  • rosdoc2: To generate C++ package documentation using Doxygen and Sphinx.

The whole process is automatized with the use of GitHub Actions.

docs.title: Deployment with GitHub Actions
docs.text:
The CI/CD workflow automates the process of building and deploying documentation to GitHub Pages. The key steps in .github/workflows/ci.yaml are:

  1. Clone configured repositories

    • The workflow reads repositories.yaml and clones each listed repository into ./repos/.
    • Add or remove repositories from that file to control which repositories are documented.

  2. Generate repository pages:

    • scripts/gen_repository_pages.py creates a page for each repository listed in repositories.yaml.
    • Each repository page contains two subsections: one for Python packages and one for C++ packages.
    • The C++ subsection links to the rosdoc2 output generated for that repository.

  3. Generate C++ Documentation:

    • Uses rosdoc2 to generate documentation for C++ packages found in the configured repositories.
    • The script searches for package.xml files under ./repos/ and identifies packages that use rosdoc2.
    • For each identified package, it runs rosdoc2 build to generate HTML documentation, which is stored under a repository-specific output directory.

  4. Move Python packages to src:

    • Copies Python packages found within the configured repositories into the src/ folder to prepare them for MkDocs documentation generation. This is done by checking for the presence of ament_python in each package.xml file.

  5. Build Documentation:

    • Runs MkDocs to generate static documentation from the source files.
    • All the configs are set in the mkdocs.yaml file.
    • mkdocs build clears the content of the site/ directory, builds the content inside the docs/ directory and processes with mkdocstrings the source code present in src/ directory. The output will be in the site directory.
    • Custom navigation is generated dynamically based on Python module structure by the gen_ref_pages.py present in the script/ folder.

  6. Add Additional Files to Site:

    • Copies the generated C++ documentation to the site directory for deployment.

  7. Deploy with ghp-import:

    • Deploys the content of site/ to GitHub Pages using the ghp-import tool.

    Danger

    ghp-import will DESTROY the gh-pages branch. This script assumes that gh-pages is 100% derivative. You should never edit files in your gh-pages branch by hand because you will lose your work.

Warning

Make sure that informations that are not meant to be public are not included in the ./docs folder or ./site folder The workflow will make the content of the ./docs folder and ./site folder public.

docs.title: Linux/Mac
docs.text:
Install Foxglove studio here and create an account.

To remove the corrupted configs and restore the docker CLI config to default Run the following command: 

sudo rm ~/.docker/config.json
Now clone the repository and enter its folder. To obtain the docker image you can pull it from our dockerhub account, first login with: 
docker login -u ubmdriverless -p <redacted>
then to pull: 
docker pull ubmdriverless/f1tenth:latest
Alternatively you can build the image yourself with: 
docker build -t f1tenth-ubm-sim -f Dockerfile .
This will take a long time, around 10-30 minutes. You only have to do it once! Now start the docker container. 
docker compose up
And in as many other terminals as you want to access the simulation run: 
docker exec -it ubm-f1tenth-sim-1 /bin/bash
In one of these terminals bring up the simulation: 
launch sim.py
This command will launch the simulator and open a websocket at ws://localhost:9090

Now that the simulator is up, you can see it by connecting to the websocket at localhost:9090. Open Foxglove studio, log in and select Open connection... on the left panel. Then select Rosbridge in the popup window and make sure that the address is ws://localhost:9090, then click Open.

The main window is the 3D Panel, here you will see a 3D rendering of the data being published by ROS. To view the car click on the 3D panel, then on Panel in the left side-bar, here you can select which topics to view, make sure that Display frame is set to map, then scroll down to Custom layers and click on the three dots to add a URDF (this will be the 3D model of the car), in the URDF settings select Topic as source and /ego_robot_description in the Topic value.

If you are seeing a bunch text and arrows on top of the car, those are the car's transforms, you can hide them in the Transforms section.

Setting the Color by value of the /scan topic to range is advised.

For more info on how Foxglove works refer to the official documentation.

You will see the car and the track! In another one of the Visual Studio Code terminals start up the control stack: 

launch control.py
In another one of these terminals send virtual telecommand signals: 
press_circle
This starts the pure pursuit algorithm and the car will move. The telecommand to stop the car is: 
press_L1
To shut it down, go to the first terminal, the one you started the container with "docker compose up" and press ^C. Next time you wish to code, open VSCode in the correct directory, start docker and connect with Tiger VNC.

docs.title: Windows
docs.text:
For compatibility, it runs within WSL. This is a linux virtual machine provided by Microsoft that runs with near bare metal performance. Open a powershell prompt and install WSL: 

wsl --install
To make sure wsl uses Ubuntu as the default distribution: 
wsl -s Ubuntu
Now open wsl by typing: 
wsl
By default, you are put in a mount on your C: drive. For read/write performance, we will create a folder in your linux home. 
cd ~
mkdir  F1Tenth
cd F1Tenth
Now we set up github to clone the repository in this directory using SSH keys, since passwords are deprecated. 
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "your_email@example.com"
Press enter to accept the default file location. Set a password. Copy your SSH key: 
cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
Go to https://github.com/settings/ssh/new and name your key, then paste it and click "Add SSH key". Now you can clone the repo: 
git@github.com:ubm-driverless/ubm-f1tenth.git
Install Foxglove here and create an account.

Do not close the powershell but go back to your Windows desktop, we have Docker Desktop and Visual Studio Code to install: https://docs.docker.com/desktop/install/windows-install/ https://code.visualstudio.com/download Open Docker Desktop, go to general settings and ensure that "Use the WSL 2 based engine" is checked. Go back to your powershell. Navigate inside the repo and open it in Visual Studio code. 

cd ubm-f1tenth/
code .
This is your development enviroment. Cool! Now to install ROS2 in a docker container, use a new terminal within Visual Studio Code. This ensures it is the correct directory and also in WSL. It's perfectly fine to run this in a new terminal if the vs code one is not working. It might be solved by rebooting.

To obtain the docker image you can pull it from our dockerhub account, first login with: 

docker login -u ubmdriverless -p <redacted>
then to pull: 
docker pull ubmdriverless/f1tenth:latest
Alternatively you can build the image yourself with: 
docker build -t f1tenth-ubm-sim -f Dockerfile .
This will take a long time, around 10-30 minutes. You only have to do it once! Now start the docker container.

Now start the docker container. 

docker compose up
And in as many other terminals as you want to access the simulation: 
docker exec -it ubm-f1tenth-sim-1 /bin/bash
In one of these terminals bring up the simulation: 
launch sim.py
This command will launch the simulator and open a websocket at ws://localhost:9090

Now that the simulator is up, you can see it by connecting to the websocket at localhost:9090. Open Foxglove studio, log in and select Open connection... on the left panel. Then select Rosbridge in the popup window and make sure that the address is ws://localhost:9090, then click Open.

The main window is the 3D Panel, here you will see a 3D rendering of the data being published by ROS. To view the car click on the 3D panel, then on Panel in the left side-bar, here you can select which topics to view, make sure that Display frame is set to map, then scroll down to Custom layers and click on the three dots to add a URDF (this will be the 3D model of the car), in the URDF settings select Topic as source and /ego_robot_description in the Topic value.

If you are seeing a bunch text and arrows on top of the car, those are the car's transforms, you can hide them in the Transforms section.

Setting the Color by value of the /scan topic to range is advised.

For more info on how Foxglove works refer to the official documentation.

You will see the car and the track! In another one of the Visual Studio Code terminals start up the control stack: 

launch control.py
In another one of these terminals send virtual telecommand signals: 
press_circle
This starts the pure pursuit algorithm and the car will move. The telecommand to stop the car is: 
press_L1
To shut it down, go to the first terminal, the one you started the container with "docker compose up" and press ^C. Next time you wish to code, start WSL, open VSCode in the correct directory, start docker and connect with Tiger VNC.

docs.title: When to Use colcon build
docs.text:
• After Cloning a New ROS2 Package or Project: If you’ve cloned a new ROS2 package or project into your workspace, run colcon build to compile it.
  • After Modifying Code or Configuration Files: If you make changes to source code or configuration files, you need to recompile using colcon build.
  • After Modifying CMakeLists.txt or package.xml: Any changes to these files require recompilation.
  • When Adding New Dependencies: If you add new dependencies, use colcon build to update them.
  • To Perform a Clean Build: Use colcon build --cmake-clean-cache to remove the CMake cache and rebuild from scratch.

docs.title: Command:
docs.text: colcon build

docs.title: Useful Options:
docs.text: • --packages-select <package_name>: to compile only a specific package.

docs.title: Additional Notes
docs.text:
• Rebuild Docker Environment: Rebuild the environment only if modifications are made to the Dockerfile.

  • Change Map: To change the map used in the simulation, modify the sim.yaml file located in the f1_tenth_gym_ros directory.

  • Control and Speed Profiles:

  • Modify control.py only in the TUM_node.
  • Create a speed profile (only if it doesn't exist already).
  • Adjust lines 21 and 22 in raceline.py if needed.

When changing a map change: control.py, raceline.py, f1_tenth_gym_ros/config/sim_yaml, launch_config.yaml
